newsitem.title: FRANCE: MEPs vote for more comparative advertising.
newsitem.headline: MEPs vote for more comparative advertising.

text.p: Advertisements which directly compare branded products, such as washing powders, will be seen more frequently following a vote by the European Parliament on Wednesday.
The 626-member assembly approved at second reading a European Commission proposal to harmonise rules on comparative advertising in the 15 member states but made some significant changes.
Under the codecision procedure, the Parliament and the EU's Council of Ministers jointly decide changes in advertising laws.
EU ministers have already agreed a common position but Parliament asked for further changes.

One major change put forward by the Parliament's environment committee will allow comparative advertising -- under which a salesman can claim that tests show his product to be superior to that of competitors -- only when the person carrying out those tests has given his consent.
The advertiser would assume liability for the tests.
Another amendment introduced by the Parliament seeks to ensure that goods are not advertised in a way that infringes the registered trade mark of a similar product.
The Parliament went against the advice of its rapporteur and said that products which have a regional name, like champagne, can only be compared with other champagnes.
It said that such adverts should not be allowed to present goods as replicas of products with trade marks, such as McDonald's hamburgers.

The Parliament also approved an amendment under which national markets would be controlled by national bodies with an EU self-regulatory body only becoming involved in the event of cross-border disputes.
